The Team + The Role

Pendo’s Customer Engineering team is the technical backbone of the pre- and post-sales customer motion. The team brings together work that has historically sat across Customer Success, Technical Account Management, and Solutions Engineering into one full-lifecycle technical owner. Customer Engineering helps customers connect technical execution to business outcomes and realize the value of their investment in Pendo.

As a Senior Customer Engineer, you own strategic and complex Enterprise accounts across acquisition, implementation, adoption, expansion, and escalation. You lead technical strategy for complex deployments, resolve ambiguous customer challenges, and partner closely with account teams to drive retention, expansion, and customer value. Your impact extends beyond your own accounts through playbooks, coaching, repeatable fixes, and workflow improvements that raise the capability of the broader Customer Engineering team.

This is a remote role supporting a West Coast territory. 

What this looks like day-to-day

• New customer acquisition and selling: Partner with Account Directors on pre-sales motions for new customer acquisition, product expansion, and expansion across lines of business. You identify customer pain, craft and deliver tailored demos, and lead technical evaluations through requirements gathering, success criteria, installation guidance, and hands-on workshops.

• Complex implementations and value realization: Lead onboarding for strategic customers, including planning, implementation, integrations, and training. You build customer-specific implementation playbooks, guide complex deployments with executive visibility, and ensure customers realize value during onboarding and over time.

• Adoption, expansion, and growth: Identify opportunities to expand adoption across underutilized features, untapped products, and new lines of business. When adoption stalls, you diagnose root causes, design a path forward, and connect technical work to measurable business outcomes.

• Technical escalation: Serve as an escalation point for complex technical challenges raised by other Customer Engineers. You resolve ambiguous problems with multiple variables and tradeoffs, involving Product or Engineering only when truly needed.

• Team capability building: Build playbooks, document repeatable fixes, coach peers, and improve how Customer Engineering work gets done across the team. You use AI tools to accelerate content creation, surface patterns across accounts, and share practical workflow findings with the broader team.

• Early account impact: Assess account health, risks, stakeholder relationships, and the highest-priority problems to solve within your portfolio. You establish trust with Account Directors and customer stakeholders, then independently lead complex customer interactions that move accounts forward.

• Quarterly business outcomes: Drive measurable improvement in customer health, retention, expansion, and technical resolution across strategic accounts. You contribute reusable frameworks, playbooks, or processes that other Customer Engineers use and become a trusted advisor to Account Directors on account health and technical strategy.

Who You Are

Beyond the qualifications, we hire through a specific lens. These aren't buzzwords; they're the things we'll actually look for in how you talk about your work.

See yourself at Twilio

In this role, you will build the foundational AI/ML capabilities that power intelligent engagement experiences for Twilio customers - letting any application, human or AI agent, or channel know who a customer is, what they have done, and how best to reach them.

Qualifications

We’re looking for a Talent Acquisition Specialist who gets curious when a profile is hard to find. Someone who enjoys digging into unfamiliar talent markets, figuring out where the right people are, and finding creative ways to reach them, whether that means a specialized industry expert or a SaaS hire.
You’re naturally curious, know how to turn an unfamiliar profile into a smart sourcing strategy, and take ownership of your pipeline from first search to signed offer. Most importantly, you want your work to have a real influence on who joins Azumuta and how we grow.
If that sounds like you, this could be your seat.
⚙️ About Azumuta

Manufacturing is going through its biggest transformation in decades, and we’re right at the center of it.
Since 2016, Azumuta has helped leading manufacturers across Europe and North America digitize their operations. Now we’re taking that further with AI that generates work instructions automatically, assists operators in real time, and removes repetitive administrative work.
We’re not simply digitizing old processes. We’re rethinking how manufacturing gets done.
And as we grow, the people we bring on board will determine how far we can take that mission. That’s where you come in.
🚀 What You’ll Be Doing

• 
Own searches from the start. Get to the heart of each role, understand the recruitment priority, challenge assumptions where needed, and align with hiring managers on the candidate profile and sourcing strategy before starting your search.

• 
Run the full recruitment cycle. Take ownership of sourcing, screening, interviewing, case assignments, candidate follow up, and offer negotiations. Whether you’re hiring for a highly specialized profile or a more familiar SaaS role, you bring the same level of rigor and care.

• 
Create a candidate experience that feels like Azumuta. Make sure every candidate gets a transparent, engaging, and respectful experience, whether they ultimately join us or not.

• 
Become a trusted partner to hiring managers. Advise them on recruitment best practices, help sharpen candidate profiles, train them in competency based interviewing, and support them in making better hiring decisions.

• 
Get creative with sourcing. Use tools, networks, communities, partnerships, and your own curiosity to reach people who are not actively looking. Keep experimenting with new approaches and continuously improve how we find specialist and hard to reach talent.

• 
Know your talent markets. Build an understanding of where the best candidates are, what motivates them, and how the market is evolving. Turn that knowledge into better searches and smarter hiring decisions.

• 
Help build our employer brand. Contribute to national and international recruitment campaigns and initiatives that make the right people curious about Azumuta.

• 
Use data to get better. Track recruitment activity and pipeline performance, identify what is and isn’t working, and turn those insights into concrete improvements.

💜 What’s In It for You
We’re a small team doing big things in a market that’s ready for change. Join us and you’ll have a real seat at the table, meaningful ownership, and the opportunity to shape the team behind Azumuta.
That means:

• 
Impact from day one. The people you bring in will directly influence our growth, and your ideas will help shape how we recruit as we scale.

• 
Room to build. This isn’t a role where every process has already been defined. You’ll have the freedom to experiment, improve our sourcing approach, and help build a recruitment function that can grow with the company.

• 
A scale up environment with solid roots. Work in a fast paced international company where autonomy, ownership, and new ideas are genuinely encouraged.

• 
A fun, ambitious team. Join colleagues who are building Azumuta’s next chapter together, with plenty of milestones and questionable dad jokes along the way.

• 
A visible role in our employer brand. Represent Azumuta at events and initiatives and help strengthen our presence in the tech and manufacturing ecosystem

• 
Around 3 years of recruitment experience, with strong hands on sourcing experience and a track record of looking beyond the obvious channels.

• 
Experience recruiting niche, specialist, or hard to find profiles, beyond standard SaaS or tech roles. When there’s no obvious talent pool, you know how to map the market and build a search strategy from scratch.

• 
A genuine hunter mindset. You enjoy research, outreach, experimentation, and the challenge of finding someone who isn’t sitting in every recruiter’s LinkedIn search.

• 
Strong judgment and curiosity. You ask the questions needed to really understand a role rather than simply working from a job description.

• 
A direct and transparent communication style. You give candidates and hiring managers the real picture, including when it isn’t necessarily what they want to hear.

• 
A strong sense of ownership. You manage your searches proactively, keep things moving, and don’t wait to be told what comes next.

• 
The ability to work autonomously and stay organized in a fast moving scale up environment where priorities can evolve quickly.

Ready to find the people who will build what’s next?
